D is the correct answer. Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn only occurs if the mother is 'incompatible' with the foetus. This means that the mother must be group A or B and the foetus must be group O. It is highest when the mother is group A and the foetus is group O. This is because group A antigens are only partially hidden by H antigens, meaning that the mother's B-cell epitopes are more exposed and more accessible to B-cells. The correct answer is D. The foramen ovale is a part of the septum transversum which is a part of the floor of the primitive heart tube. During development, this structure is a flap that allows blood to pass from the right to the left atrium before birth, bypassing the immature lungs. After birth, when the lungs fill with air and oxygenated blood is produced, the pressure in the left atrium exceeds that in the right and the flap is closed. The crista terminalis is the remnant of the septum transversum after the foramen ovale has closed. If the flap does not close, it results in an atrial septal defect (ASD).
